title: Manga 'Hagure Idol: Jigoku-hen' Gets TV Anime in Winter 2027
content:
WWWave Corporation 's Deregula animation label opened an official website for a television anime adaptation of Rui Takatou 's Hagure Idol: Jigoku-hen ( Booty Royale: Never Go Down Without a Fight! ) manga on Friday, revealing the main cast, staff, and a commemorative visual (pictured). The anime series will premiere in January 2027.

Cast Misora Haebaru: Hisako Toujou ( Boushoku no Berserk ) Sarah Goujima: Nao Shiraki ( Kimi to Boku no Saigo no Senjou, Aruiwa Sekai ga Hajimaru Seisen ) Yun-Hui Choi: Natsumi Murakami ( Love Live! Nijigasaki Gakuen School Idol Doukoukai ) Nene Koori: Hikaru Iida ( Kimi wa Meido-sama. )

Staff Director: Takashi Andou ( Inu ni Nattara Suki na Hito ni Hirowareta. ) Series Composition: Eiyo Kurosaki ( Ingoku Danchi ) Character Design: Ryuuji Iwata ( Kanojo no Tomodachi ) Chief Animation Director: Morimori ( Ai no Utagoe wo Kikasete key animation) Art Director: Minoru Aota ( Android wa Keiken Ninzuu ni Hairimasu ka?? ) Art Design: Do Kim Hoan Tran ( Marika-chan no Koukando wa Bukkowareteiru ) Color Design: Riku Saitou ( Egao no Daika color specification) Director of Photography: Tomohiro Hayashi ( Hitozuma no Kuchibiru wa Kan Chuuhai no Aji ga Shite ) Editing: Tomohiro Hayashi Sound Director: Akinori Shiba ( Ookii Onnanoko wa Suki desu ka? ) Sound Production: Object Music: ZincP Producer: Deregula Studio: Raiose Production: WWWave

Takatou began serializing the ecchi comedy manga in Bessatsu Manga Goraku from April 2014 to December 25 that year. The series later moved to Manga Goraku Special in March 2015. The manga went on hiatus in September 2022 and resumed serialization in March 2024, before moving to the Goraku Web! in June 2025. Nihonbungeisha published the 19th volume on April 28.

A spin-off manga, titled Hagure Idol Jigoku-hen Gaiden: Princess Sarah , was serialized on the Goraku Egg platform from April 2015 to December 2015. The first and final volume was released in February 2016.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the manga in English under its Ghost Ship mature reader imprint in 2-in-1 omnibus editions in December 2020. The 17th and 18th volume went on sale on July 14.

A live-action movie adaptation, produced by Sedic Deux, premiered in Japan in September 2020.

Synopsis Eighteen-year-old karate expert Misora Haebaru moves to Tokyo to pursue her dream of becoming a famous singer. Unfortunately, her sleazy handlers trick her into the adult entertainment industry instead. Her only way out is to survive a martial arts tournament where she must fight her way through one hundred lustful male opponents. If she loses, she will pay the ultimate erotic price! (Source: Seven Seas Entertainment)

title: Amahara's 33 Years Old Single Girl Knight Captain Manga Gets Anime
content:
Digital Shokunin annoucned on Friday that it is producing an anime adaptation of manga creator Amahara 's 33-sai Dokushin Onna Kishi Taichō (33 Years Old Single Girl Knight Captain [sic] ) manga. The project's YouTube channel is streaming a music video with a song titled "Boogieing Dance Kishi" (Boogieing Dance Knights) with vocals by Sekka, composition and arrangement by Suzumi, and lyrics by Sekka and Suzumi. ( WARNING: The video below may not be safe for work )

The sex comedy fantasy manga centers on the titular 33-year-old girl and knight captain Mail, as well as her friends, who all suffer from exploitative work conditions and are too busy to sate their sexual desires. They spend what little free time they have drinking and pleasuring themselves.

Amahara launched the manga in KATTS ' online adult manga magazine Ananga Ranga in October 2015, where it is still ongoing irregularly, with every new chapter often only being one or two pages long. Flex Comics published the manga's fourth compiled book volume on January 15.

Amahara and masha 's similar sex comedy fantasy manga Interspecies Reviewers ( Ishuzoku Reviewers ) first ran as a special one-shot in Kadokawa 's Monthly Dragon Age magazine in July 2016, and then later launched in the Dra Dra Sharp# section of the Nico Nico Seiga website in August 2016. Kadokawa published the manga's 12th compiled book volume on October 9. Yen Press licensed the manga and released the 11th volume on April 28.

The manga inspired a television anime premiered in January 2020. Funimation removed the series from its streaming service later in January, stating the company "determined that this series falls outside of [its] standards." The company stated it decided to take down the series altogether instead of altering the content. Amazon Prime Video removed both the English-dubbed and English-subtitled versions of the anime in the first week of February 2020. Right Stuf later licensed and released the anime uncensored on Blu-ray Disc in December 2021.

Amahara serialized the original web manga version of The Idaten Deities Know Only Peace ( Heion Sedai no Idaten-tachi ) manga on the Neetsha website, but abruptly halted it in May 2016. Coolkyoushinja launched a remake of the manga in Hakusensha 's Young Animal magazine in August 2018. The manga caught up to the older online version of the manga in early 2023, and ended in August 2024. Hakusensha released the manga's ninth and final volume in October 2024. Seven Seas Entertainment is releasing the manga in English, and it released the ninth volume in November 2025. The manga inspired an anime that premiered on Fuji TV 's Noitamina programming block in July 2021. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired in Japan.

title: Despite Fan Backlash, Dragon Ball Super Remake Is One of the Biggest Hits of Fall 2026
content:
Netflix’s weekly ranking chart reveals that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is one of the biggest hits of the year. The highly anticipated remake became a massive disappointment after the release of Episode 3, which was even before the main battle between Goku and Beerus. This is the first anime that the Dragon Ball franchise released after Daima , which was the final project of Akira Toriyama. Considering the franchise’s popularity, it’s no surprise that the hype was greater than ever, even if the latest anime was a remake rather than a sequel. The animation studio claimed to fix the biggest issues with the original anime adaptations, including the animation quality and the pacing.

However, so far, the anime remake has been rather disappointing considering how it keeps removing fan-favorite scenes while also having exaggerated filters and jarring visuals that are somehow worse than the original version. However, while the anime finds itself in the middle of the controversy, Netflix Tudum reveals that the anime gathered more than 2.2 million views between October 19th and 25th, around the time the anime had only released two episodes. It also ranked ninth among the top 10 global non-English shows, which again proves how much the franchise is loved despite having faced so much backlash.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Continues to Face Controversy With New Episodes

The anime has released four episodes so far, but the battle between Goku and Beerus has yet to begin. While his Super Saiyan God form has been revealed in the latest episode, the anime continues to receive fan backlash for the same reasons . The tone of the story and the light-hearted moments have been shifted in the remake version, which doesn’t appeal to many fans. This is only the first arc of the remake, and the anime still has to adapt the Resurrection F and Universe 6 Arcs. While the remake stayed true to its promise of closely following Toriyama’s version of the story, it feels unnecessarily concise, without the scenes that made the series so loved. Not to mention that the anime leans too heavily on slow-motion pans and still frames, instead of fluid animated sequences, which is another reason why the anime keeps receiving fan backlash.

What’s Next for Dragon Ball Super ?

Earlier this year, Dragon Ball Super confirmed its return with a brand new season that will continue the story after the Tournament of Power Saga. Also known as the Moro Arc, the story follows Goku and Vegeta as they join the Galactic Patrol to fight a prison escapee, Moro, a 10-million-year-old magic user who consumes planets. However, the animation studio has yet to share any details on the anime’s return, considering how the remake has grabbed all of the attention this year. On the other hand, fans are still awaiting the manga’s return with Toyotaro taking over the helm. The extra chapter released in 2025 concluded the Super Hero Saga, so we can expect the manga to return with a brand new adventure.

Do you think Dragon Ball Super: Beerus can turn things around after the Battle of the Gods Arc? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: 3 Anime to Watch If You Miss Avatar: Seven Havens
content:
The Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise keeps expanding as the latest animated series was released after 12 years to explore the exceptional worldbuilding and the captivating characters. After its exciting announcement in 2025, Avatar: Seven Havens premiered in October this year and reached its conclusion in the same month. The series released batches of three to four episodes every Friday starting from October 9th. The first season wrapped up in Episode 13 before confirming that the animation series will return with a brand new season. The story this time centers around twin Earthbender sisters, Pavi and Nisha, as they navigate a world where the Avatar is feared among the masses rather than being treated as a savior.

While Paramount has officially confirmed that the series will have four seasons, the next season hasn’t shared any updates so far. It’s only been a week since the first season wrapped up, which means fans will have to wait at least a few months, or even longer, to get updates on Season 2. However, while you wait for the series to return , there are plenty of exciting anime shows set in unique worlds that can keep you busy in the meantime. If you’re looking for stories centering around mystery and magical adventure, these three will be perfect for you.

3) Heavenly Delusion

Heavenly Delusion is one of the wildest and darkest anime of the 2020s, but it never gained the attention it deserved. Similar to Seven Havens , it’s set in a post-apocalyptic world as the protagonists navigate through the dangers in order to reach a place called Heaven. This sci-fi mystery takes place 15 years after a massive disaster struck human civilization, and now dangerous man-eating monsters roam around the land. As humanity is on the brink of collapse, an isolated facility shelters children and keeps them away from potential harm. The anime, produced by Production I.G., received acclaim right after its debut but was never confirmed for a second season. Maru and Kiruko are two young survivors who wish to live in a peaceful world, but as their search for Heaven continues, the story unfolds their past burdens and secrets as they try to find a better place in the broken world.

2) Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood

There are hardly any anime series that can come close to the exceptional worldbuilding, layers of mysteries, and complex characters like Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood . The story is not only popular for its incredible story, but also for having one of the most satisfying endings in Shonen history. Fans of Avatar: Seven Havens will love this anime as it focuses on siblings’ bond while also dealing with the cost that comes with power. The 64-episode-long series follows the tale of two brothers who embark on a journey to search for the legendary Philosopher’s Stone and reclaim what they lost. However, amid their search, they get entangled in the centuries-long scheme that has been taking place in their country, as everything seems to be connected to the dark truth behind the legendary object. While the manga received an anime adaptation in 2003 , it severely deviated from the original manga, but this reboot saved the franchise.

1) Moribito: Guardian of the Spirit

Hardly any anime fan these days even remembers or talks about this forgotten masterpiece. The story spans across 26 episodes, following the themes of survival and redemption as a young woman decides to save the life of a prince. Much like Seven Havens , this underrated anime features the same grounded, martial-arts fight choreography, powers related to the spiritual realm, and heavy moral dilemmas as the fate of the world hangs in the balance. Set in a land that resembles medieval Japan while also incorporating Chinese and Mongolian culture, the story follows the journey of Balsa, who saves a young prince, Chagum, from an assassination attempt. She later accepts the request of Chagum’s mother to save his life after learning that the boy’s father, the Emperor, is targeting him. As the duo’s journey continues, the truth behind Chagum’s identity and the prophecy that threatens the entire kingdom comes to light.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime you’d like to recommend that shares similar vibes to Avatar: Seven Havens ? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Ninja Skooler Anime Unveils Pilot Film, Images, Song
content:
Makoto Kimura 's BLUE RIGHTS anime planning company unveiled on Friday a pilot film and images for Kinema Citrus ' original anime project Ninja Skooler . The company also digitally released the featured song "Knots" written and performed by Takashi Iwami .

The company describes the story:

Rappa is an orphan who idolizes fictional ninja. One snowy night, he falls from a rooftop and is saved by a real ninja named Okachimachi and his master. Rappa turns up at their door asking to become an apprentice, and the three begin living together as a family. Years later, Rappa throws himself into training to become a ninja who can protect the town. The children who look up to him gather at the master's traditional Japanese candy shop, a place where he can laugh with family and friends. Rappa thinks these days will last forever, but he sees Okachimachi tending to their retired master and catches a glimpse of the pain the master has kept hidden...

Shunsuke Takarai is directing and supervising the Ninja Skooler with character designs by Hami . The anime is based on a concept by Kinema Citrus .

The staff also includes:

• Key Animators: Yuka Kuroda, Franziska van Wulfen, Shunsuke Takarai

• In-between Checker: Aoi Higuchi

• In-between Checker Assistance: Studio BUS, Min Kyung-ae

• In-betweeners: Gift-o'-Animation (Keito Suzuki, Mizuki Hori), Studio BUS (Min Kyung-ae, Park Kyung-sook, Min Su-in, Shin Sun-mi, Jang Yun-young, On Nuri Park)

• Color Key Artist/Coordinator/Checker: Hiroaki Kaguchi

• Finishing: Hiroaki Kaguchi, Anitus-Kobe, YOSHIKI Eri, Studio BUS (Na Jong-ah, Kim seo-young, Kim Jung-hye, Kim Yeon-mi, Kim Eun-kyeoung, Baek Sung-hee, Kim Mi-yeon, Lee Jeong Mi)

• Background Art: Hami, Shunsuke Takarai

• Compositing Director of Photography/Editor: Shinichirō Miyazaki

• Sound Director/Mixing: Haru Yamada

• Sound Effects: Tōru Noguchi

• Audio Production: Sound Team Donjuan

• Music: Nanatsukaze(PIKASONIC＆nakotanmaru)

• Studio Management: Kōji Sone, Naoko Matsumoto, Michiko Akima, Tomoka Kuwahara, Naruhito Mitsuwaka

• System Management: Takanori Sunaga, Shigeo Miyagi

• Creative Department Management: Kensuke Aoshima, Miyu Inoue

• Translation: Hiromi Hasegawa, Jorge Herrera

• Vehicle Coorporation: Komatsu Tsusho Co., Ltd.

• Animation Producers: Muneki Ogasawara, Satoshi Wada

• Production Assistant: Satoshi Wada

• Animation Production/Based on concept by: Kinema Citrus

Kinema Citrus originally announced the anime at the Anime Central event in Rosemont, IL in May 2024.

title: Mashle: Magic and Muscles Manga Gets Live-Action Film on March 19
content:
An early teaser visual announced on Wednesday that a live-action film of Hajime Kōmoto 's Mashle: Magic and Muscles manga will open on March 19, 2027. Warner Brothers and Fuji TV are overseeing the project, and CREDEUS is producing. TOHO will distribute the film.

The tagline on the visual above reads, "It's finally time for a movie adaptation, Mashle."

Both Viz Media 's Shonen Jump service and Shueisha 's MANGA Plus service published the manga digitally in English. Viz Media is also releasing the manga in print. Shueisha describes the manga:

This is a world of magic where magic is used for everything. But deep in the forest exists a young man who spends his time training and bulking up. He can't use magic, but he enjoys a peaceful life with his father. But one day, his life is put in danger! Will his muscular body protect him from the magic users who are out to get him? Powerfully trained muscles crush magic as this abnormal magical fantasy begins!

The series launched in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine in Japan in January 2020, and ended in July 2023. Shueisha published the manga's 18th and final compiled book volume, as well as a fan book, in October 2023.

title: 3 Fall 2026 Anime That Take Fans Back to the 2000s
content:
Three anime in Fall 2026 perfectly capture the nostalgia of 2000s anime while delivering that classic shonen feel. The anime industry began to flourish with the emergence of classic shonen anime, many of which were released throughout the 2000s. Series such as One Piece , Naruto , Bleach , and many others captured the essence of shonen anime and defined the era.

Modern anime, especially shonen, have increasingly embraced realism, with darker protagonists and storylines becoming the standard. As a result, anime that retain the charm and feel of older series have become increasingly rare. Fortunately, Fall 2026 has not one or two, but a total of three currently airing anime that perfectly capture this nostalgic appeal.

3) Black Clover Season 2

Black Clover is one of the most quintessential shonen series of all time, embracing all the classic tropes and elements of older shonen anime, and it might just be the last new series to do so. The anime returned in Fall 2026 with its second season after five years of silence, adapting the final two arcs of the series. Black Clover has often been dubbed the successor to Naruto , with its protagonist being an oddity who possesses the optimistic energy that drives the entire narrative.

With its new season positioning its main character, Asta, as someone capable of standing against the greatest evil threats with his newfound power, the series perfectly captures the feel of older shonen anime entering their final climactic arcs. It boldly embraces this energy as the main characters and their allies continue to receive new power-ups, face greater challenges, and overcome them. Arguably, no other anime in 2026 delivers the perfect blend of action, comedy, and 2000s anime nostalgia quite like Black Clover .

2) Psyren

If an anime needs to deliver a 2000s vibe, then it might as well come from the 2000s, and that is exactly what Psyren fulfills. The anime adaptation of Psyren is a miracle , considering that the manga was cancelled during its run in the late 2000s after reaching only 100 chapters. The first episode is more than enough to highlight what makes Psyren a perfect shonen series that captures the feel of older anime. It achieves this through several elements, starting with its protagonist. Ageha Yoshina is exactly the kind of shonen protagonist one would expect from a series of that era.

He is bold and loud, yet lacks a purpose in life, making him somewhat reminiscent of Bleach ‘s Ichigo Kurosaki. Meanwhile, the narrative’s entire setup is rooted in the 2000s, with elements such as telephone booths reflecting the era in which the story takes place, all of which is further amplified by the studio’s faithful anime adaptation. However, the anime isn’t entirely rooted in the past, as its central premise revolves around a survival game, adding a modern element to the story as well. This makes Psyren a perfect choice for Fall 2026, blending the classic shonen vibes of the 2000s with the appeal of modern anime.

1) Dragon Ball Super: Beerus

Dragon Ball is known as the father of shonen anime, having laid the foundation for countless series that followed throughout the 2000s and even today. This is what makes any anime from the Dragon Ball franchise capable of capturing the spirit of that era, when anime was flourishing, and almost every new anime fan was getting into the medium through Dragon Ball . What makes Dragon Ball Super: Beerus even more nostalgic is that it is a remastered version of the 2015 Dragon Ball Super anime , further amplifying that nostalgic appeal.

It takes fans back to the era when the Buu Saga had come to an end, and the franchise was preparing to take an entirely new direction. In general, any anime from the Dragon Ball franchise, especially for those who grew up watching it, can transport fans back to that nostalgic era, regardless of whether they were born in the 1990s or 2000s. It delivers a sense of nostalgia that arguably no other anime franchise can match.

title: PlayStation 5 Reaches Over 97 Million Shipments
content:
PS5 reached over 90 million shipments last February, and reached over 80 million shipments in August 2025. It surpassed 50 million in sales in December 2023.

As of July 2021, Sony had sold over 10 million units of the PS5 worldwide since its launch, making the PS5 Sony 's fastest-selling console. Sony had sold over 20 million units of the PS5 worldwide as of June 2022. The PS5 had crossed 30 million units in sales in January 2023, and then crossed the 40 million mark in July 2023.

Sony raised the price of its PS5, PS5 Digital Edition, and PS5 Pro consoles, as well as its PlayStation Portal peripheral, beginning on April 2, due to "continued pressures in the global economic landscape." The company raised the price of the PlayStation Plus online gaming subscription service for new customers in select regions beginning on May 20.

Sony announced on July 1 that it is ending physical game disc production for all new games on PlayStation consoles starting in January 2028. All new game releases starting in that month will be digital only. This does not affect games that have already been released or that will ship prior to January 2028 as discs. The company cites this decision as an adaptation "to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs."

The PS5 launched in the United States, Japan, Canada, Mexico, Australia, New Zealand, and South Korea on November 12, 2020. The console launched in most of the rest of the world on November 19, 2020. The PS5 got a new, smaller model intended to replace the old model throughout November to early December in 2023 in various territories.

The PlayStation 5 Pro console shipped in November 2024. The PS5 Pro features PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, 120 FPS, advanced ray tracing, 2TB of SSD storage, upgraded GPU with "28% faster memory", and AI-driven upscaling to improve image clarity.

Sony released a new model for the PS5 Digital Edition in Japan that only has Japanese language support in November 2025. It is cheaper than the multi-language Digital Edition model, at 55,000 yen (about US$355). The current Digital Edition model for the PS5 sells at 72,980 yen (about US$471) in Japan.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Clearly Sets Up a Third Movie, Despite New Sequel Claiming “Everything Ends Here”
content:
The ending of Godzilla Minus One in 2023 heralded the arrival of a sequel in a way that created more excitement than any other tease in the franchise’s history. Following his defeat, the heart of Godzilla began to sink to the ocean floor just as it started to regenerate and begin to beat again, signaling his return. In theory, the series could have left it there, but after the blockbuster success of the film and winning the first-ever Academy Award in the history of the franchise, a sequel felt mandatory. With Godzilla Minus Zero now here three years later, we found ourselves wondering again.

Picking up two years after the previous movie, Godzilla Minus Zero not only brings back some of the beloved characters from the original (with plenty of fresh ideas sprinkled in) but also some newcomers that radically change the film’s plot as it moves forward. On a bigger scale, Godzilla Minus Zero also delivers some major new additions to this branch of the franchise on the kaiju side of things . All of which culminates in a movie that clearly isn’t the end. Naturally, Godzilla Minus Zero spoilers follow .

Godzilla Minus Zero Ending and Sequel Setup Explained

It’s worth noting that Godzilla Minus Zero has been marketing itself in a very peculiar way, with the official description including two key sentences: “There is no third time. Everything ends here.” Ahead of the movie’s release, it sounds quite definitive, but after seeing the movie, it becomes quite absurd, because Godzilla Minus Zero clearly ends in a way that sets up a third chapter in the series.

The larger plot of Godzilla Minus Zero hinges on the arrival of a new kaiju, featuring a brand new take on Ghidorah , an alien species that crash-landed on Earth and assumed the form of a dragon-like creature after meshing together some of the wildlife it encountered in its first form. Though they’ve stayed busy, the newly formed Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau, headed up by Minus One ‘s Kenji Noda, must lead a group of scientists eager for a way to stop the new monster.

After a failed attempt to kill Ghidorah ends up causing the kaiju to mutate (and grow his signature extra heads and tails), the team realizes that perhaps the best way to combat the beast will be fighting fire with fire, planning to use technology by Kanji Murakami, a biologist who has crafted a technology that can be used to lure (and potentially control) Godzilla out of hiding. Key to this tech, though, is Noriko Shikishima, whose encounter with Godzilla in the first movie has left her partially mutated, with Godzilla cells growing out of her body (and her eye color changed). Unbeknownst to everyone, though, Murakami’s plan to control Godzilla isn’t an altruistic one, as he has hopes for revenge against the United States following his family’s death in Hiroshima.

Godzilla Minus Zero ‘s big finale not only sees the two kaiju fight, with the titular monster coming out victorious after a bloody fracas, but the end of their battle is far from the conclusion of the story. With Ghidorah defeated, the United States Army moves in to seize control of Murakami’s technology, hoping to one day exploit it to weaponize Godzilla one day. Knowing that his plan to use the King of the Monsters against the US would go against the wishes of his family, he burns it all to save it from falling into their hands.

As Godzilla walks back into the ocean and swims away to live another day, Godzilla Minus Zero is still not done, including with teases for the future. At the film’s end, Kōichi and Noriko decide that because of her G-Cell mutation, she’ll likely be a target for the United States, forcing them to go on the run. The film ends as they, along with their adoptive daughter, go into hiding.

If Godzilla still being alive and wandering back into the ocean wasn’t a sign that there was still more story to tell, the two main characters running off to live another day makes it all doubly obvious. Once again, this brings us back to the wild marketing plot for Godzilla Minus Zero, “There is no third time. Everything ends here.” The movie itself makes it CLEAR that this movie isn’t the ending, but that said, Toho and director Takashi Yamazaki haven’t committed to another film.

After the success of Godzilla Minus One , Yamazaki was quickly courted for other projects, including in Hollywood, with his next movie confirmed to be Grandgear for J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot and Sony Pictures. Speaking with The Hollywood Reporter , Yamazaki opened up about the potential for a new film to follow Minus Zero, saying it’s “fifty-fifty at this point” whether he’ll return for another story.

“I’m quite satisfied and happy with the current ending we have,” Yamazaki said. “It entrusts the interpretation to the audience in terms of how they want to receive it and what they want to walk out of theaters with. That being said, if Godzilla Minus Zero is my last Godzilla film, that would make me a bit sad…At some point in my career, I would love to revisit Godzilla and see how we can expand this world.”

Based on how Godzilla Minus Zero ends, there’s no chance he doesn’t at some point down the line. That said, Toho selling the new movie as the end of this saga means these two movies can, in theory, exist as their own continuity while the studio potentially explores other Godzilla ideas. Until Yamazaki decides to return, the story for this branch of Godzilla lore appears done…even if it’s far from over.

title: Crunchyroll to Stream Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Anime's English Dub on November 12
content:
Crunchyroll announced on Thursday that it will begin exclusively streaming the English, Spanish, and Portuguese dubs for the Dragon Ball Super: Beerus television anime series on November 12 at 11:00 a.m. EST. New dubbed episodes will premiere weekly. The company streamed an English trailer:

The dub casts (featuring returning members) include:

English

• Sean Schemmel as Son Goku

• Christopher R. Sabat as Vegeta

• Jason Douglas as Beerus

• Ian Sinclair as Whis

Spanish

• Mario Castañeda as Son Goku

• René Garcia as Vegeta

• José Luis Orozco as Beerus

• Arturo Castañeda as Whis

Portuguese

• Wendel Bezerra as Son Goku

• Alfredo Rollo as Vegeta

• Marcelo Pissardini as Beerus

• Felipe Griñán as Whis

Crunchyroll is simultaneously streaming the anime in Japanese with English subtitles on October 11 in the United States, Canada, Latin America including Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, India, Southeast Asia, and Europe. Hulu is also streaming the anime as it airs. Netflix began streaming the series in the U.S. on October 17, and and October 14 in selected areas/countries.

The first episode also screened in advance at the Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Special Panel at New York Comic Con on October 8.

The staff for the new anime includes:

• Composition and Direction Arrangement: Matsuto Seya

• Animation Character Design & General Animation Director: Tadayoshi Yamamuro

• Editing: Eiichi Nishimura

• Compositing Director: Yōsuke Motoki

• Music: Norihito Sumitomo

The anime again features Kōichi Yamadera as Beerus.

MEGATERA･ZERO performs the opening theme song "ONOGAMI," and VK Blanka performs the ending theme song "Kan Peki No Peki."

Akio Iyoku stated the work started a few years ago and is an "enhanced" edition of the Dragon Ball Super anime that features a reconstruction of the story, and includes new and redrawn cuts.

The official announcement of the anime stated:

The project features extensive new cuts, revisions to existing scenes, a complete re-rendering of all footage, newly recorded dubbing with added score and sound effects, and a full reconstruction of the story. Living up to the name ENHANCED, this edition employs the latest visual expression to deliver greater power and immersion across all scenes, especially the battle sequences. The result is an ENHANCED edition that expresses Akira Toriyama 's original idea and worldbuilding more accurately, that will be broadcasted with highly satisfying quality.

The anime staff stated, "the anime Dragon Ball Super ... is set to begin anew as Dragon Ball Super: Beerus in Fall 2026."

The staff describes the story:

Several years have passed since the fierce battle against Majin Buu, and Earth has finally regained a brief moment of peace. At the same time, Beerus, the God of Destruction, awakens from his long, deep sleep. Even Kai and Supreme Kai, aware of Beerus's overwhelming power to destroy entire planets, watch his awakening with great fear… Meanwhile, Beerus hears rumors of a Saiyan who defeated Frieza—and suddenly appears before Goku.Targeted by Beerus, the strongest being in the universe, Earth is in grave danger. Thus begins an Earth-shattering cosmic battle between the God of Destruction and Goku and his allies—a conflict that will shake the entire universe.

Dragon Ball Super premiered in July 2015 and aired for 131 episodes until March 2018. Funimation and Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and Funimation released the series on home video. Funimation debuted the English dub to its streaming service in December 2016. The English dub premiered on Adult Swim 's Toonami block in January 2017.
